description: A screen that draws one pixel per sample: the position jacks say where and the colour jacks say what colour, and the picture builds up as the position moves

params.text: Reads the three colour jacks as red, green and blue in one setting and as hue, saturation and value in the other
Sets what voltage range the colour jacks cover: -5V to +5V in one position, 0V to 10V in the other
Sets what voltage range the position jacks cover: -5V to +5V in one position, 0V to 10V in the other
Held down, fills the whole screen with mid grey
Opens a separate resizable window showing the same picture, redrawn about thirty times a second
Sets how many pixels across and down the screen has, 1 to 1000

inputs.text: Channel 1 is the horizontal position of the pixel and channel 2 the vertical; patching this leaves the separate X and Y jacks unread
The horizontal position of the pixel to draw; it is unread while the two-channel position jack has a cable in it
The vertical position of the pixel to draw; it is unread while the two-channel position jack has a cable in it
Channels 1, 2 and 3 carry the three colour components; patching this leaves the separate colour jacks unread
The red or hue of the pixel to draw, depending on the colour-format switch; it is unread while the three-channel colour jack has a cable in it
The green or saturation of the pixel to draw, depending on the colour-format switch; it is unread while the three-channel colour jack has a cable in it
The blue or value of the pixel to draw, depending on the colour-format switch; it is unread while the three-channel colour jack has a cable in it

notes: one pixel is drawn per audio sample, so a whole picture only appears once the position has been swept over the screen; a PathGenerator is what usually does that
a position that falls outside the screen draws nothing rather than wrapping round
this module has no outputs; the picture goes to the panel and to the separate window, not to a cable
changing the resolution clears the picture
